Blueberry's general drawdown structure is mixed, not uniformly static: Prime is static, whereas the 3-Step and Instant variants use trailing limits, with an eventual lock for Instant. For funded synthetic plans purchased from 8 October, profits from trades lasting under five minutes are excluded from rewards, a different rule from prohibited tick scalping. The company explicitly permits VPN/VPS only with a dedicated static IP, warns that shared or rotating addresses may pause access, and publishes restrictions on multiple household accounts sharing an IP. These clauses need product/date-specific application, not a blanket VPN prohibition. The earlier official Prime parameters and Trustpilot withheld-rating incident remain in the file. set.auditSummary: Deep audit (17 November 2026): IC Funded's current 2-Step Professional rules specify a 10% Step 1 and 5% Step 2 target, 5% daily limit calculated on end-of-day equity, 10% fixed overall drawdown, and three active days per evaluation step. Current Terms section 12 prohibits latency/price exploitation, artificial target-meeting trades and certain automation; it gives the operator broad rights to cancel rewards on violations. The terms explicitly distinguish simulated capital from live market funds; KYC and jurisdictional eligibility still apply. Unlike 2-Step, the Instant program advertises at most 80% reward share, so a single firm-level figure must not be read as every product's default. Spread, platform execution and bank/on-chain payment evidence were not independently tested; no Trustpilot manipulation allegation is inferred.

set.verdict: Lark Funding publishes useful product and withdrawal FAQs, but its 'instant' model does not mean unrestricted daily withdrawals: later payouts use a 30-day cycle and a $40 fee applies. set.auditSummary: Official-source deep review dated 17 November 2026. Lark Funding allows VPNs and VPSs for trading while discouraging them because network anomalies can trigger additional scrutiny; it explicitly prohibits VPN usage during KYC/AML identity checks, where it may lead to refusal or a breach. Standard 1-Step, 2-Step and 3-Step payout requests follow 14-day cycles, unlike the Instant product whose first request is on demand but subsequent withdrawals are 30 days apart. There is a $100 minimum withdrawal and a stated $40 charge for each payout; processing is advertised within three business days, not guaranteed bank receipt. The firm excludes Myanmar, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Belarus and other jurisdictions, but absence from an exclusion list alone does not confirm local regulatory permission in India, China or Singapore. Its homepage has previously shown contradictory product-card reward/drawdown labels, so account-specific checkout terms take precedence. Trustpilot's older 4.3/5 snapshot is a public review aggregate, not proof of independently settled rewards, and PropRadar did not test spreads, slippage, account opening or receipts.

set.auditSummary: Deep audit (17 November 2026): Moneta Funded Ltd is disclosed in Saint Lucia (2025-00532); its September 2026 contract defines simulated funds and account-specific rules, not deposits at Moneta Markets. Its program comparison spans 1-Step Daily, 1-Step, 2-Step, Instant, Instant Pro, Phoenix and Sprint. The comparison marks news trading disallowed on the ordinary 1/2-Step and Instant models but allowed on Instant Pro and Phoenix, with material differences in loss limits and first payout. For Instant, it states a 15%/20% consistency threshold; clause 5.1F of the current PDF calculates best realized trading day divided by total realized P&L in that payout cycle, delaying payment when breached. The PDF also allows automatic closing or excluding profit above an Instant Pro per-day cap. At the time of review, the public general-rules page described 1-Step/Phoenix as 6% static while the comparison presented its generic One-Step as 5% trailing: this may reflect product variants or stale copy, so obtain the exact program/checkout document in writing. Advertised 14-day/on-demand reward cycles are not authenticated customer payout evidence; no account or spread was tested by PropRadar.

set.auditSummary: Detailed official help-centre audit on 17 November 2026. A reward request requires 14 days since the previous payout (or seven with a paid weekly add-on; first cycle starts with first trade), no open trades, no pending/limit orders, a within-cap consistency ratio, and at least $100 after the profit split. Trading goes to view-only while the request is processed. A separate official article explains that a funded breach, including a drawdown or unauthorized automation discovered at payout review, permanently closes the account and voids simulated gains including gains accrued before the breach. The May 2026 multiple-IP policy permits different devices/addresses but expects geographical IP-region consistency: changes can prompt travel evidence, a passport stamp or live location video; this must not be misreported as a universal VPN/VPS ban. The 10 November eligibility guide lists UAE and several other restricted countries and explicitly cautions that successful checkout does not establish the legal right to receive services. Source dates and model-specific thresholds are given so users can verify before purchase. The earlier Trustpilot rating-withheld notice and firm-reported $1M+ payout counter remain separately labeled; neither proves payment verification. PropRadar's commercial relationship has no role in this assessment, and no firsthand payout/spread test occurred.

set.auditSummary: The official challenge agreement (17 November 2026 review) offers a more useful risk picture than the sales homepage alone. Section 7.4 prohibits different strategies in evaluation versus funded simulation and cross-account hedging; section 7.5 leaves classification of prohibited trading to the firm's discretion. Section 8.7 permits additional risk profiling after successful assessment and potentially rejecting funded account access, while saying the assessment fee or credits remain refundable in that specific case. Section 9 conditions access on identity verification and cites an 80% trader share, contrasting with the 'up to 90%' homepage claim (upgrades or conditions were not independently established). Section 10 lists restricted jurisdictions including Japan, Pakistan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Afghanistan and others; this is published company eligibility, not a legal opinion or proof that a checkout accepts another country. The site claims 24-hour rewards, but no bank-level payout verification, real trading test or measured spread data was obtained.

changelog.summary: First in-depth trading-rule audit using current official FAQ and All Rules. Standard share starts at 50%, not headline 90%; top-level or conditional 90% Lock is different, forfeits higher scaling and requires milestone first. Outside scaling events, payouts may be requested monthly (weekly at the top/Lock), and an invoice must be submitted within 30 days of target or profit share is forfeited. Trading inactivity of 42 days terminates an account. The FAQ says Iran, North Korea and OFAC countries excluded; US clients cannot use Metaquotes. No independent withdrawal, spread or license verification performed.

set.verdict: The Concept Trading advertises profit sharing up to 90%, but its published default for every model is 50%; 90% needs top-level progression or the optional Lock Rule, which sacrifices further scaling. Its FAQ additionally requires a timely invoice to avoid loss of earned profit share, while inactive prop accounts can terminate after 42 days. Published eligibility and payout schedules are not substitutes for proof of independent trader payments.
set.auditSummary: PropRadar's 17 November 2026 desk audit read the official current FAQ, All Rules and Terms for program-level catches. The firm's standard profit-share arrangement begins at 50% on every model; 90% is offered at a top program level or through the 90% Lock Rule. Lock activation is unavailable on Foundation and Intern accounts, requires first reaching the chosen scaling milestone and receiving its normal split, and prevents further account scaling after election. Once on Level 1 or higher, rewards are triggered by a scaling target; otherwise the FAQ permits one withdrawal per month, rising to weekly at the highest level or with the Lock Rule. Most importantly, the official FAQ requires a profit-sharing invoice within 30 days after hitting the scaling target or the entitlement is forfeited; a six-week/42-day inactivity period also terminates the account. The FAQ excludes Iran, North Korea and US-sanctioned jurisdictions and says US residents cannot use Metaquotes platforms, though other platforms are accepted. It describes static drawdowns varying by plan, not a single universal percentage. These rules and the firm's public financial-service authorisation claims have not been independently verified via a regulator in this pass; no hands-on execution, spread comparison or verified bank payout exists.

set.verdict: Tradicave is listed as closed in a current specialist directory, and tradicave.com does not provide an authenticated working checkout. Historic community reports raise payout questions, but there is no verified company dissolution or independently established refund disposition. PropRadar preserves the dossier as a closed commercial-brand archive and strongly discourages purchases under this name.
set.auditSummary: 17 November 2026: Tradicave is marked CLOSED by a prop-firm specialist directory updated in November 2026, while its former tradicave.com website is unavailable. That supports a conservative commercial closure classification but does not establish formal winding-up of a particular legal entity. Prop Firm Match's historical unlisted listing includes multiple independent-looking 2024 user posts alleging refused payout requests and copy-trading-rule disputes, alongside at least one user testimonial claiming a completed payout within three days. Neither kind of post contains a retrievable independent bank confirmation tied to the named recipient, so PropRadar does not convert them into verified payout evidence. A secondary listing mentions Prop Trade Tech LLC; without a first-party contract or official corporate record linking that name to Tradicave, its legal identity remains unverified. The original terms, refund policies and successor responsibilities were not available; historical Trustpilot rumours cannot be substituted for a domain-matched current profile. Risk score falls from 44 to 33 because an apparently inactive seller, missing legal details and unresolved historical payment complaints create clear buyer uncertainty.
